highlights.title: Donald Trump really wants Tim Cook to run Nvidia
highlights.description: Jensen Huang resigned this morning as Nvidia's CEO following reports of affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Right now, the company is being led by its CFO on an interim basis. But President Donald Trump is already throwing around one person he thinks should take over the chipmaking giant: former Apple CEO Tim Cook, who stepped down from leading the company on September 1st and moved into an executive chairman role. highlights.title: Abrupt End to Nvidia’s Jensen Drama Leaves Unanswered Questions
highlights.description: Jensen Huang’s long-running Nvidia drama ended on a cliffhanger with the news of the CEO’s resignation Thursday morning. We’re going to have to wait a while for the scriptwriters to figure out the next installment of this thriller. At the moment, we’ve got far more questions than answers: What happened between Sunday, when the board said it had confidence in Huang, and Wednesday night when Huang quit (as Nvidia revealed in a securities filing today)? What role did the Trump administration play i

highlights.title: Inside Jensen Huang's Final Hours as the CEO of Nvidia
highlights.description: At the end, Jensen Huang looked broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted. After weeks spent denying the allegations of infidelity and fighting to remain in his job as Nvidia Corp.’s chief executive officer, his surrender late Wednesday night was unconditional. Huang’s usual take-charge demeanor had evaporated, according to a person familiar with the situation, and he’d started using phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”

highlights.title: ByteDance to Buy Back Shares at $400 Billion Valuation
highlights.description: ByteDance, the Chinese owner of TikTok, is planning to buy back up to $6 billion worth of shares from existing investors at a valuation of about $400 billion, a 20% increase in the valuation used in its last buyback a year ago, according to a letter to shareholders seen by The Information and a person familiar with the plans. highlights.title: Sources: President Trump urged Jensen Huang to keep fighting for his job in a Tuesday call; aides say Trump saw the company as essentially too big to fail (New York Times)
highlights.description: New York Times: Sources: President Trump urged Jensen Huang to keep fighting for his job in a Tuesday call; aides say Trump saw the company as essentially too big to fail — The president called the Nvidia chief on Tuesday, continuing a pattern of supporting him even as the spy scandal was intensifying.

highlights.title: Nvidia May Face Employee Churn, Analyst Says
highlights.description: Patrick Moorhead, CEO and Chief Analyst at Moor Insights and Strategy, says Nvidia could face months of employee churn as uncertainty lingers over its CEO search. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: Nvidia Is Not a Normal Company Having a CEO Issue: Everson
highlights.description: Carolyn Everson, a board member at Coca-Cola, Disney and Under Armour and a senior advisor at Permira, discusses how boards respond to allegations involving executives. Everson speaks with Romaine Bostick and Jess Menton on “The Close.” (Source: Bloomberg)
